title: A Mixtape for the Playlist
premise: Wendell Dravenmoor, a scholarship student counting down to graduation at Ashgrove Academy, discovers her late grandmother's recipe box holds encoded directions to the school's hidden memory vault, where the elite have been storing and stealing students' recollections for generations. When her own memories begin vanishing, she must enter the Academy's two championships—one public and meaningless, one secret and everything—to reclaim what was taken from every scholarship kid before her. She wins the hidden contest by refusing its terms, shattering the vault and returning stolen memories to their owners, though she loses some of her own past forever. In the end, she records what remains on a mixtape, choosing which memories to keep rather than letting power decide for her.
about_author: Paloma Delacroix is a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's letters, photographs, and forgotten keepsakes. She writes young adult novels about the things institutions keep and the people they erase.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Sorting her grandmother's belongings in the academy attic storage, Wendell finds recipe cards whose instructions describe locations, not dishes—each one mapping a corridor of Ashgrove. When she follows one, she witnesses the headmaster extracting a memory from a failing senior. The beat is dread blooming into resolve: the countdown to graduation just became a countdown of a different kind.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. To access the restricted wing where the vault sits, Wendell enters the public academic decathlon, befriending rival Theo, whose brother graduated hollow-eyed and half-remembering. Training scenes intercut with her first memories slipping—a birthday, a face. The emotional beat is uneasy alliance: trust as strategy, then as something realer.

chapters.title: Everything the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with an interlude from the headmaster. Inside the vault, Wendell finds decades of stolen childhoods filed like preserves—including her grandmother's, revealing grandma was a rebel who hid the map in plain sight. Caught by the headmaster, she's offered her memories back in exchange for silence. The climax ignites as she refuses and triggers the championship that does matter: a contest of will inside the vault itself.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell wins by overloading the vault with her own freely given memories, collapsing the archive and flooding the school with returned pasts. Some of hers are lost in the flood—she grieves them without bitterness. Graduation arrives; she hands Theo a mixtape labeled with what she chose to remember. The final beat is quiet triumph: identity as curation, not possession.
